title: Share of the Annual Pool a Membership and Patronage Equity Revolvement Draws for a Year Come Due
content:
The board revolves a larger share where a year has genuinely come due and carries a balance worth paying.

**The larger share.** Where no revolvement payment stands against the recorded eligibility year and the credits that year carries stand above the class's minimum equity balance, the share is 15 in the hundred.

**The ordinary due share.** Where no revolvement payment stands against that year and the credits it carries stand at or below the class's minimum equity balance, the share is 12 in the hundred.

**Otherwise.** The share is the percentage of the equity the class's annual pool fixes, as the class schedule of Membership and Patronage Equity carries it.

## Points of judgement on hypothetical figures

| Revolvement payment standing against the recorded eligibility year | Credits that year carries | Class minimum equity balance | Share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | 1450.00 | 25.00 | 15 in the hundred |
| none | 25.00 | 25.00 | 12 in the hundred |
| none | 18.00 | 25.00 | 12 in the hundred |
| 300.00 already paid | 1450.00 | 25.00 | the class's own annual pool share |

**On the second line.** Credits standing exactly at the class's minimum equity balance stand at or below it, so 12 in the hundred is the share and not 15.

**On the last line.** Once a revolvement payment stands against the recorded eligibility year, neither of the first two readings holds, whatever the credits come to.

**Worked.** Credits of 7000.00 drawn on give 1050.00 at 15 in the hundred and 840.00 at 12 in the hundred.
